summary: All nine original jobs succeeded. Windows and Linux contracts, actual registered business paths, independent vectors and four hosted network experiments passed within their recorded scopes. This does not qualify the entire rewrite or physical targets.

limitations: Private cfg(test,Linux) prototype uses Quinn rebind_abstract after out-of-band fixture agreement; no production migration negotiation
Production path epoch remains one; no simultaneous proposal, lost ACK, bounded epoch drain, grant renewal or old-v15 semantic change
Same original PathGrant, Permit and transport group; each real preauthenticated relay has its own signed TransitGrant and unchanged deadlines/quotas
Fresh phase-tagged OS file bytes traverse one pinned inner QUIC stream after all old physical sockets release and old interfaces are down
No business endpoint SessionPermit proof, actual FileRead worker, input/media/TCP recovery, SDK signaling or full AC22 qualification
RTT, congestion and logical PLPMTUD trajectories are observations; Quinn local_address_changed changes CID and sends ping without resetting these estimates
NRD fragmentation adapts logical packets up to 1400 bytes onto outer QUIC fixed at 1200 bytes; logical PMTU is not physical dynamic PMTU convergence
Four isolated kernel namespaces and actual netem loss/delay/rate, no NAT/public Internet/installed device acceptance; private credentials are excluded from artifacts

Successful business scope is owned Linux 1:1 UDP address mappings with peer-restricted ingress; the forced destination-dependent case proves refusal only, without external-router, general symmetric NAT, CGNAT or IPv6 NAT qualification
Actual signed remote SessionPermit, SDK signaling, bilateral ICE and pinned Quinn run; no screen, input injection, audio or installed Windows acceptance
FileRead frames carry a complete owned random 256KiB payload in both directions; no file browser, filesystem grant, download/resume or file worker claim
Both original legacy and ICE physical sockets must be rebound after explicit owner cleanup; success cannot fall back to legacy
Management uses unchanged loopback-only HTTP development policy with namespace-local transparent TCP forwarders; no SDK TLS rules changed
Credentials, identities, ICE passwords and signaling payloads remain in private temporary storage outside artifacts; captures contain UDP only
No two-relay or NAT topology, real LAN or target device qualification
No SDK signaling/discovery, TLS/WSS fallback, new network routing or migration qualification
FileRead uses production client/server with a fixture adapter approving one real file
Success/cancel isolate teardown packets to measure independent local ExplicitExit; peer-close separately verifies unisolated code-0 close maps to host Revoked
No screen capture, OS input injection, installation, performance, 24h or UU acceptance
Environment guards prevent accidental local execution; GitHub run/job/artifact records remain authoritative
No bilateral ICE/STUN nomination, consent or same-socket hole-punching qualification
No public/external NAT, dual relay, multi-hop discovery or path migration
Inner QUIC handshakes and complete 1280-byte IPv6-shaped payloads run through the production routed adapter; no TUN injection
No business SessionPermit endpoint proof, actual FileRead worker or SDK signaling; framed bytes are transport checks only
Physical captures show encrypted outer UDP and actual SNAT tuples; they do not decrypt inner Initial packets
Credentials/seeds remain in an owned temporary fixture outside artifact output; no installed-device or full acceptance qualification
